items.title: A chart component library, shared by all eight surfaces
items.detail: `public/shared/charts.js` (786 lines) exists with all five named primitives plus `sparkline` and the scale helpers, and is exercised by `test/charts.test.js` (50 tests). It reaches 2 of the 8 surfaces — `public/co/app.js:11` (static) and `public/app.js` (lazy, at `:1280` and `:1705`, the latter also pulling the workflow wires that import it). Of the primitives the audit named as uncalled, `heatmap` now has a call site (`public/app.js:1300`, the seasonal calendar); `lineChart` and `stackedBar` still have none outside the library. `barChart` has three (`public/app.js:1745`, `public/co/app.js:415`, `public/workflow/wire-playback.js:168`), `sparkline` one (`public/co/app.js:478`) and `smallMultiples` one (`public/app.js:1766`).
items.note: public/shared/charts.js with lineChart, barChart, stackedBar, heatmap, sparkline, smallMultiples, legend, caption and divergingBar — the last because scenarios drew a two-pixel div bar and approximating it with barChart loses the zero anchor. 206 tests across the charts and viz suites. All primitives return SVG strings, take no DOM and are used by every surface that draws.

items.title: Render uncertainty as geometry, not as a footnote
items.detail: Shipped as `public/shared/viz-uncertainty.js`. `sensitivityBandChart` draws the band **hatched**, never as a gradient — a soft ribbon is the confidence-interval visual grammar, and hatching survives greyscale and colour blindness. Edge labels read 'sensitivity low'/'sensitivity high'; a test asserts `p10`, `p90` and 'percentile' appear nowhere in the SVG, table or caption. The disclaimer is in the return value, not an option, so the wiring step copies the geometry and the sentence together, and a record claiming `calibrated_uncertainty: true` throws rather than being relabelled. Rendered on the console over 16 live risk records, with the module's own caption verbatim beneath. Guarded by `test/charts.test.js`, `test/viz-uncertainty.test.js`.

items.title: Time-slider playback of hazard history
items.detail: Shipped as `public/shared/viz-playback.js`. The console steps 292 hazard events and 10 alert events through `buildFrames`, auto-bucketed to weeks over a 364-day span, with `frameSummary` per frame and `peakFrame` for a 'Jump to peak (2026-09-28, 69 active)' control. The scrubber is `<input type="range" id="playbackStep">` (`public/index.html:546`). The chart discloses that 68 of 78 records carry no end date and stay active for the rest of the timeline — so a rising count is the archive accumulating, not floods worsening. Guarded by `test/viz-playback.test.js`.

items.title: Map → chart → record drill-down, with a `/explain` endpoint
items.detail: Shipped as `GET /api/v1/explain/{id}` (`src/routes/provenance.js:54`), which resolves a record to its source run and lineage rows. The audit's before-state read: no such route existed then, a map click opened `openDetailDialog` (`public/app.js:3781`) rendering the record's own fields as a flat `<dl>` — no time series, no underlying records, no per-term coefficient breakdown. The route ships the `:id` form rather than the audit's `/explain/:kind/:id`, because the id alone resolves the kind. The adjacent evidence defect is fixed too: `calibrationReport` (`src/analytics.js:1222`) is routed from `/api/v1/assessments` (`src/routes/events.js:85`), which is the calibration metadata, not the equation endpoint.
items.note: Every record the console opens now explains itself: map markers, map record list, alert rows. `explainRecord` (public/shared/viz-explain.js) renders the arithmetic; GET /api/v1/explain/{id} supplies the provenance the client cannot compute — the source run and the lineage row. A record naming no source run returns 200 with `provenance.known: false` and a sentence saying so, because absence of provenance is a fact about the record, not a reason to withhold it.

items.title: Month × year seasonal calendar heatmap
items.detail: Shipped. The month × year matrix is on the console with the flood/alert overlay the item asks for: 78 hazard and alert records bucketed to months across the ENSO grid's own columns (`seasonalCalendar` at `public/app.js:1269`). It is a calendar rather than a single anomaly number because the structure an operator reads for is seasonal — a warm phase peaks around November-December and decays through the following spring. It does **not** difference against a per-month climatological median: the published anomaly is already a departure from a 30-year base, and differencing twice reports the spread of the series under study rather than its position. It does not interpolate an un-ingested month. Guarded by `test/seasonal-calendar.test.js`, `test/charts.test.js`.

items.title: Forecast-versus-observed verification charts
items.detail: Shipped as `public/shared/viz-verify.js`. `pairForecasts` joins 54 `precipitation_forecast` records against flattened archive dailies on region-day; `reliability` and `reliabilityDiagram` (`public/shared/viz-verify.js:294`) render the result. **The store holds zero archive records, so all 54 pairs are `pending` (28) or `no_outcome` (26) and none is verified.** The console renders 'Not yet measured' with the per-status counts, why the gap is missing outcomes rather than a good result, and the event definition it will use — and draws no diagram. An honest empty state is the deliverable here; a chart of invented data would not be. Guarded by `test/viz-verify.test.js`.

items.title: Offline-first drill-down and cached map tiles
items.detail: All five changes shipped. The precache list is a computed breadth-first closure of the real import graph (`public/sw.js:111`, guarded by `test/web-chw-offline.test.js:437`); the queue throws unless IndexedDB confirms the write (`submitOrQueue` at `public/shared/runtime.js:424`); `/api/v1/*` GETs are network-first with an API cache fallback under a tested eviction cap; the offline marker is read on the success path (`public/shared/runtime.js:348`, which also reads `x-lindela-stored-at`), so a cached success is distinguishable from a live one; and raster basemap tiles have their own bucket (`CACHE_POLICIES.tiles`, `public/sw.js:66`, 400 entries / 7-day TTL, routed at `:165`). The audit's before-state: three of the five had shipped, there was no tile cache, and no surface read the offline header. Per-panel staleness is rendered (the CHW and focal-point staleness banners).
items.note: Four read buckets in the service worker: a named record gets its own (60 entries, 7-day TTL) so the console's 30-second poll cannot evict the districts a health worker visited; the map's hazard/flood/road layers get a third (48, 2-day); and raster basemap tiles get a fourth (400 entries, 7-day TTL) routed on the `/api/v1/basemap/tiles/` prefix, because a pan paints about two dozen tiles and they would flood the 48-entry map bucket. A miss is never an empty panel: 503 with a code, and `cached: false` distinguishes 'no data' from 'no data because I never fetched any'. Hits carry x-lindela-stored-at and x-lindela-stale-seconds stamped when written, not read off Date. Two defects fixed en route: activate would have deleted the detail bucket on every version bump, and stale hits were rewrapped under the stored response's own content-encoding.

items.title: Colourblind-safe and high-contrast themes
items.detail: The secondary-encoding half shipped and is guarded: `hazardShape` (`public/app.js:1356`) and `severityDash` (`public/app.js:1373`) are applied to every map and legend severity class, with six tests in `test/web-console.test.js:214-262` asserting distinct shapes, distinct dash patterns and that an ungraded record is not painted as "low". The palette half did not: `public/tokens.css` is a single dark `:root` with no deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia check, no high-contrast mode, and no `prefers-contrast`/`forced-colors` theme; `scripts/check-a11y.mjs:24` audits WCAG contrast but only against that one theme.
items.note: [data-theme] on <html>, applied purely at the token layer: `:root, :root[data-theme=dark]` keeps the shipped palette, plus light, high-contrast, and two @media mirrors that are the only correct path at first paint. Precedence is explicit choice > prefers-contrast > prefers-color-scheme > dark, persisted, with localStorage throwing degrading to 'no preference'. check-a11y measures all three themes across all eight surfaces — 24 assertions, all passing — and applies each theme the way a choice actually arrives, by writing localStorage before the page script. Colour-vision separation simulated (Machado 2009, severity 1.0): worst pairwise CIE76 dE dark 8.7, light 7.4, contrast 10.0. Severity carries word + glyph + a hatch whose density rises with severity, so nothing depends on hue alone.

items.title: Shareable, deep-linked, per-role dashboard state
items.detail: The console encodes and restores six filter/time-window params — `sev`, `source`, `range`, `cold`, `alerts`, `workflow` — through `syncFiltersToUrl`/`restoreFiltersFromUrl` (`public/app.js:2867-2921`), called from 5 sites including boot at `:4185`; scenarios has a share token in the URL hash plus a copy button. Missing: map extent and selected feature are not in the URL, there is no per-role saved default view anywhere (`public/shared/runtime.js` exports no view-config API), and no test exercises any of it — the only `replaceState` reference in `test/` is a stub. Shipped, unguarded.
items.note: public/shared/view-state.js, pure and testable, so a share link can be asserted without a browser. Three properties a URL has to have, because a link is a claim about what someone was looking at: the encoding is deterministic (map transforms are floats, and a link that differed per run would copy something the sender never saw); fields equal to the role default are not written, so a link narrows a role default rather than overwriting it; and it is versioned, with a link from a newer build decoding its known fields and carrying an advisory. ROLE_DEFAULTS covers seven roles. The share button appears only once the view differs from the default. Round trip verified in a browser. test/view-state.test.js, 17 tests.
